newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK GOVERNMENT CONSIDERS TAXING FOREX LOANS - IMERISIA.
newsitem.headline: GREEK GOVERNMENT CONSIDERS TAXING FOREX LOANS - IMERISIA.

text.p: The Greek government plans to tax forex loans to try to contain liquidity and ease inflationary pressures on this front, financial daily Imerisia said today.
Making forex loans more expensive will reduce demand for them and restrict liquidity obstructing a further reduction in inflation, the paper said.
The new tax will be valid for all forex loans and will be calculated on the unpaid portion of the loan and not the basic interest rate.
Imerisia said the proposal was brought to the government by Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos and has been accepted by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou.
Papandoniou is reported to have ordered a feasibility study on the revenues the tax is expected to bring in.
The tax is expected to have an impact on interest rates for forex loans and on the tax to be calculated on the amount of the loan.
Forex loans have to date not been subject to taxation, unlike drachma loans which carry a Special Banking Tax (EFTE) and a 1.0 percent charge.
